## 固定收益市場主線

9月23日，美國各期限附息公債全面下跌。油價反彈、美國企業景氣調查強勁，推升市場對聯準會繼續升息的預期；隨後$700億5年期公債標售需求疲弱，又使跌勢加劇。彭博同日殖利率歷史資料顯示，10年期殖利率上升15.2個基點至5.115%，5年期上升16.7個基點至5.004%。標售得標殖利率為5.033%，比發行前交易殖利率高3.1個基點。5年期殖利率盤中自2007年以來首次突破5%，逆轉前一交易日短天期公債的喘息走勢。

前一天，美伊外交進展的希望曾推低油價；23日布蘭特原油期貨反彈3.86%，收在每桶$103.08。伊朗總統仍對荷莫茲海峽通行設下條件，能源供應恢復因而面臨重大障礙。美國9月綜合採購經理人指數初值達58.4，為2021年7月以來最高，新訂單增強，投入成本急升。聯準會理事Michael Barr表示，通膨風險上升，勞動市場風險則已減輕。油價、調查數據與Barr的談話，使標售疲弱之際的通膨及政策壓力更為突出。

殖利率升勢也傳至其他公債市場：週三交易報導顯示，德國與英國10年期公債殖利率分別上升9及11個基點。美元走強、標普500指數下跌；美國投資等級債利差小幅擴大，高收益債利差明顯擴大。企業仍能融資，但成本高昂。軟銀為人工智慧計畫完成約$110億美元及歐元高收益債發行，其美元債殖利率創自身紀錄。融資順利完成與借款成本高昂並存，是當日另一項鮮明特徵。

## 美國成長、聯準會政策與標售需求推高公債殖利率

前一交易日的美伊外交進展曾讓油市稍感寬慰，週三油價走勢卻再度轉緊，布蘭特原油重返每桶$100以上。伊朗總統Masoud Pezeshkian在聯合國大會表示，只要制裁及美國封鎖仍在，伊朗就不會允許船隻自由通過荷莫茲海峽。他表示願意恢復談判，但這些條件也顯示，重啟對話與重新開放這條關鍵能源航道之間仍有距離。

美國政府同時研究國內燃料供應措施。能源部長Chris Wright表示，政府正與煉油業者合作，尋求自願限制柴油出口；白宮則否認正準備實施90天出口禁令的報導。這些說法尚未證實出貨量會改變，但反映高燃料成本除外交途徑外，也已引發政策回應。布蘭特原油在紐約時間下午5點固定收益市場截止時升至$103.08，使先前因原油降價而稍獲緩解的通膨前景再度承壓。

另一股壓力來自標普全球9月美國企業調查初值。綜合產出指數由8月的56.0升至58.4，高於55.2的預測，並創逾5年新高。製造業指數由53.9升至57.0，高於53.6的市場共識；服務業指數由56.5升至58.7，也高於56.0的預期。民間經濟兩大部門同步加速，這比單一部門拉高整體數值更值得利率市場關注。

需求與產能指標也支持這項判斷。新訂單指數由55.2升至58.2，為2022年3月以來最高，製造業與服務業均有增長。未完成訂單為2022年5月以來最多，供應商交貨延誤則為2022年7月以來最普遍。就業增速創逾4年最快；投入價格指數由59.9跳升至66.4，為2022年10月以來最高。企業提及燃料及運輸成本，許多企業也反映薪資漲幅加快。需求增強之際，供給能力也面臨限制。

標普全球表示，這份調查所反映的情況與約5%的GDP年化成長率相符。亞特蘭大聯準銀行GDPNow估計值為5.1%，相較之下，第二季實際成長率為1.5%。PMI仍是衡量企業景氣廣度的初步調查，並非已實現的GDP數據；但產出、訂單、聘僱與成本同步加快，確實使投資人重新評估緊縮政策要多久才能使經濟放緩。

具有利率決策投票權的聯準會理事Barr為這項重新評估提供了明確的政策說法。他認為，通膨偏離2%目標的風險增加，勞動市場風險則減輕；要讓通膨及時回到目標，可能還須進一步調整政策。決策委員會前一週一致決議升息25個基點，將目標區間調至3.75%至4.00%；18名決策官員中有16人預測年底前至少再升息一次。路透社解讀Barr的談話，認為他可能主張至少再升息兩次，但他沒有指明時點。

Barr發言後，短期利率期貨反映的10月27日至28日會議再次升息機率約為70%，高於週三稍早的約55%。較廣泛的利率市場中，交換契約已充分反映未來一年升息三次、每次25個基點，對第四次升息也有相當程度的避險。兩項價格涵蓋的期間不同，卻同樣顯示調查數據與Barr談話後，市場更加重視持續升息的可能性。

白宮對繼續升息提出異議。國家經濟委員會主任Kevin Hassett主張，近期核心通膨年化率為2%，不足以支持再升息。他批評非由總統川普任命、卻主張進一步緊縮的聯準會官員，並稱主席Kevin Warsh正在管理一個異常政治化的央行；他特別點名前主席Jerome Powell與Barr。Warsh、Powell和Barr與委員會其他成員一樣，都投票支持前一週的升息。Hassett的批評凸顯對數據及政策回應的政治分歧，Barr則提出了當日聯準會方面更具體的新判斷。

下午的5年期公債標售，考驗了已在下跌的市場。這場$700億標售以5.033%得標，相較發行前交易參考殖利率5.002%，尾差達3.1個基點；在彭博自2018年起的紀錄中，這是5年期標售第二大尾差，僅次於2022年6月。投標倍數為2.21倍；間接投標人取得54.3%，直接投標人取得29.9%，交易商承接15.8%。得標殖利率為該券種自2006年以來最高。標售使當日殖利率升勢明顯加快，但並非唯一原因。

5年期殖利率盤中最多上升20個基點，突破2023年的4.99%高點。彭博盤中報導曾記錄10年期殖利率升近17個基點至5.13%，30年期則在5.4%左右交易。依彭博同日殖利率歷史資料，2年期上升14.2個基點至4.898%，5年期上升16.7個基點至5.004%，10年期上升15.2個基點至5.115%，30年期上升10.0個基點至5.401%。短天期承受較多調整，2年期與30年期殖利率差收窄4.2個基點至50.3個基點。

抗通膨公債顯示，10年期名目殖利率升幅主要來自實質利率。10年期TIPS實質殖利率上升13.2個基點至2.77%，同期限損益兩平通膨率上升2.0個基點至2.345%。油價仍是重要通膨風險，但同一來源的拆解顯示，週三名目利率重新定價，主要反映投資人要求更高實質殖利率。這與較強的成長數據、更高的預期政策利率路徑，以及持有利率敏感部位的成本提高相符。

債市以外也出現相同壓力。美元指數上升0.56%至101.10；另一項彭博美元指標上升0.6%，達7月下旬以來最高。標普500指數下跌0.75%，那斯達克100指數跌0.84%，半導體指數跌1.21%；黃金期貨下跌1.33%至$4,318.40。iShares 20年以上美國公債ETF下跌1.6%至$80.46，創收盤新低。其今年以來含配息的總報酬為負4.8%，股價本身則跌7.7%；評估持有人承受的損失時，兩者應予區分。

在週三美國公債收盤前，住房融資條件已趨緊。抵押貸款銀行家協會指出，截至9月18日當週，30年期固定房貸契約利率上升15個基點至7.12%，為2024年5月以來最高。申請總量繼前一週下降4.1%後，再減少1.5%；房貸市場指數由230.8降至227.3，再融資指數由627.1降至611.0，購屋指數由156.2降至154.9。5年期浮動利率房貸則反向下降13個基點至6.1%。固定利率上升與申請量減少，顯示美債殖利率再漲之前，住房市場已受到融資成本牽制。

財政部另宣布，依部長Scott Bessent擴大後的回購計畫，週四將回購最多$60億、距到期20至30年的公債；上限是8月原先公布$20億規模的3倍。消息公布後，長天期公債跌勢延續，報導所述30年期殖利率當時觸及盤中高點5.38%。前一次擴大後的操作中，投資人提出$105億債券，財政部在$60億上限下實際買入約$52億；官員表示，剩餘額度未用完，是因具競爭力的報價不足。國際金融協會週三認為，次級市場購債或可暫時緩解壓力，卻無法解決債務上升背後的財政因素。週四公布的是回購上限，實際買入金額仍待確定。

## 全球經濟活動與央行面對能源衝擊

經濟合作暨發展組織（OECD）的期中展望顯示，政策難題不限於美國。該組織將2026年全球成長預測由2.8%上調至2.9%，仍低於2025年的3.4%；2027年預測則由3.1%下修至3.0%。G20今年通膨預測由4.0%上調至4.1%，明年由3.1%上調至3.6%；2027年通膨預測除中國與沙烏地阿拉伯外，所有G20經濟體均遭上修。AI投資支撐近期成長估計，較持久的能源衝擊則削弱較遠期前景。

OECD預測聯準會今年還會升息一次，歐元區、澳洲及南韓將小幅進一步升息，日本也將持續緊縮；英國與加拿大央行則暫時按兵不動。美國2026年及2027年成長率預測分別為2.2%和2.1%，通膨率分別為3.6%和2.6%。其不利情境同時納入能源市場壓力、強烈聖嬰現象、政府公債殖利率上升及AI投資報酬不如預期，合計可能使2027年全球成長率下降0.7個百分點、通膨率上升1.1個百分點。這顯示資金成本提高可能放大供給及投資失利的影響，但不是該組織的基準預測。

歐元區9月企業活動數據則強化了近期成長的一面。綜合PMI由52.0升至53.1，與市場預測降至51.7相反，創逾3年新高；服務業也意外改善。德國經濟活動成長速度為2025年10月以來最快，法國為逾2年最快。標普全球的Chris Williamson認為，製造業部分強勢來自AI與國防支出，製造業和服務業的訂單也都有改善。調查顯示，能源及借貸成本雖高，歐元區經濟仍在擴張。

但這份韌性未能支撐週三的歐元。交易員增加下跌避險，歐元兌美元一度低至$1.1409，接近兩個月低點。市場報導引述存託信託暨結算公司（DTCC）資料指出，自最近一次聯準會會議以來，約60%的歐元選擇權名目金額押注歐元走弱；歐洲央行升息後，兩個方向原本大致各半。看跌部位的加權平均到期期間也延長逾10%。美國成長及利率預期轉強的同時，高能源成本威脅歐元區較遠期前景。德意志銀行分析師則持不同看法，預期全球成長韌性及美元自身的風險會限制歐元長期下跌。

歐洲央行首席經濟學家Philip Lane對通膨風險提出區分。他表示，能源價格急升迄今尚未造成明顯薪資壓力，因此價格衝擊透過薪資變得持久的證據較少。不過，他認為能源價格直到2027年中仍沿著歐洲央行的不利情境走，之後才會回到基準路徑附近。天然氣庫存約為70%，比歷史平均低16個百分點；歐元區8月通膨率已超過3%，部分經濟學家預期年底可能達4%。

Lane也提醒，不能將觀察到的市場價格直接換算成預期升息次數。表面定價似乎顯示，6月和9月升息之後還有三至四次升息；但扣除風險溢價後，他認為隱含的政策利率高點僅在明年略高於3%，並於2027年底前下降，約相當於再升息兩次。薪資尚未受到顯著推動，減輕了一條通膨持續傳導的途徑，卻未消除能源價格及低天然氣庫存帶來的風險。

英國面對的是活動放緩與財政壓力的組合。OECD預測英國2026年成長1.1%、2027年成長1.0%，平均通膨率分別為3.1%與2.6%；預期英國央行將把3.75%政策利率維持至2027年中，之後降息25個基點，同時敦促政府更積極控制並重新配置支出。經濟學家估計，利息成本與通膨上升，已使財政大臣John Healey原有的£236億財政規則緩衝空間減半。

10月28日預算案公布前，首相Andy Burnham也加入了這場討論。他重申先前所說英國不應受制於債券市場，認為國家已讓自己過度暴露於市場壓力，並主張建立更具生產力的政府。國防和社會支出均有目標之際，借款額又高於先前預測。報導所述30年期英國公債殖利率為5.76%，低於前一週接近6%的高點。週三英債殖利率上升是全球公債跌勢的一部分；Burnham的談話與OECD的警告，使預算案如何處理財政壓力更受關注。

南非央行已作出政策決定：六名貨幣政策委員一致投票升息25個基點，將基準利率調至7.25%，符合彭博調查22名經濟學家中19人的預期。總裁Lesetja Kganyago表示，央行必須在衝擊消退之際，讓通膨回到3%目標。8月通膨率由4.3%微升至4.4%；央行將2026年平均通膨預測由4.0%上修至4.4%，2027年由3.8%上修至4.0%。今年油價假設由每桶$82上調至$90，明年由$75上調至$80。

官員除最後選定的25個基點外，也討論過維持利率及升息50個基點。Kganyago表示，決策前的政策僅略具限制性，並警告規模大且持續的衝擊更可能引發第二輪影響。央行假設全球利率或國內通膨預期更高的不利情境，所需升息次數將比其他情況多一至兩次。約翰尼斯堡下午交易時段，南非蘭特跌勢擴大，貶值1.3%至約每美元16.39蘭特；10年期公債殖利率上升9個基點至8.90%。一致決議與預測上修，比升息幅度本身更清楚顯示其通膨考量。

印尼央行連續第三次會議維持5.75%利率，符合受訪36名經濟學家中33人的預期，並以外匯市場優惠措施應對外部壓力。由總裁Destry Damayanti領導的央行，將投資組合資金使用傳統避險交換契約的溢價最多降低25%，境內無本金交割遠期契約的溢價最多降低30%；資金留存越久，折扣越大。央行也繼續在境外與境內市場干預，包括在次級市場買入公債。決議後，印尼盾升值0.4%至約每美元17,800盾，當地債券維持稍早漲幅。

Destry認為現行利率足以維持穩定，但也承認當時油價已高於$100、全球通膨升溫，且聯準會可能再升息。印尼8月通膨率為3.2%，接近1.5%至3.5%目標區間上緣；銀行放款較去年同期成長13.65%，高於央行預期的8%至12%。瑞士隆奧的Homin Lee仍預測，若能源不確定性及聯準會緊縮持續，印尼央行12月將升息25個基點。因此，這次維持利率依靠留住資金的誘因與市場干預；若壓力持續，利率回應仍有可能。

新加坡則公布另一項亞洲通膨數據。8月核心消費者物價較去年同期上升2.2%，符合調查預期，為2024年9月以來最高；食品、零售及服務價格漲幅加快，整體通膨率為2.3%，公用事業及其他燃料價格上升6.1%。新加坡金融管理局與貿易主管部門認為，油價、天氣與進口成本沿供應鏈傳遞，使風險偏向上行。金管局預測今年核心通膨為1.5%至2.5%，約自2027年中起趨緩；10月中旬的下一次決策將評估是否需要再次調整匯率政策。

日本債市因銀週假期休市，須待週四重新開市，才會反映週三全球殖利率升勢。日圓兌美元連跌四天；日本央行近期升息至1.25%後，匯率走弱再次引發對外匯干預及輸入性通膨的關注。Eastspring Investments投資組合經理Rong Ren Goh另提出全球長天期債券需求可能流向何處的看法：殖利率超過4%的30年期日本公債，若透過交換契約轉成美元或其他已開發市場貨幣，避險後殖利率可能比該貨幣的可比債券高100至200個基點。他指出，日本2年期與30年期殖利率差超過200個基點，其他核心已開發市場平均約80個基點。Eastspring正透過高品質公司債與武士債增加日本超長天期曝險，同時增持較短天期美元債。這些是該經理的策略及殖利率比較；假期後的日本交易，才會提供下一個市場觀察。

## AI融資成本高昂，信用避險交易增加

軟銀週三將初步認購需求轉化為確定的融資條款。這家日本集團為AI計畫發行約$110億美元及歐元高收益債，依彭博統計成為全球最大的企業高收益債借款人。美元債包括$10億、3.5年期券，殖利率8.625%；$45億、5.5年期券，殖利率9.25%；以及$45億、7.5年後到期券，殖利率9.75%。另發行€10億的4年期及6年期債券，較長的歐元券殖利率為8%。美元債殖利率為軟銀在該市場歷來付出的最高水準，較長歐元券的殖利率也創下其同期限借款紀錄。

亞洲下午初步報價時，$100億美元債的訂單超過$300億，使軟銀得以將殖利率從初步區間調降。龐大的投機等級融資因此順利完成，但基準美債殖利率上升，最終借款成本仍高。軟銀對OpenAI的資金承諾接近$650億；除這批新無擔保債券外，也使用其他擔保及過橋融資。高盛信用策略師估計，2026年全球AI相關債券發行額超過$5,750億。軟銀債務違約保障成本本月升至2025年4月以來最高，顯示強勁訂單並未消除市場對其曝險規模的疑慮。

規模較小的資料中心建設融資，因不同風險而付出同樣高的殖利率。由Blue Owl Capital關係企業、Cedarwood Investment Group及PowerHouse Data Centers支持的開發商，為維吉尼亞州里奇蒙附近Digital Drive資料中心園區發行$11億、5年期高收益債。債券以每$1面額98.5美分定價，殖利率9.25%，比同評級債券平均殖利率高約2.7個百分點；高盛、花旗及德意志銀行主辦發行。

融資將為一座76兆瓦設施增加運算容量。該設施已依15年、總額$29.4億的合約全數租予CoreWeave，預計2027至2028年開始營運。標普給予債券BB-評級，並指出依賴單一投機等級租戶是主要風險。長期租約支持預期收入，但專案仍須在營運前取得資金，租戶的信用品質也影響投資人要求的殖利率。

成熟AI借款人的避險交易同樣增加。標普道瓊指數的Nicholas Godec引述DTCC資料指出，最近六個月市場交易的輝達債務違約保障，所對應債務達$69億，前六個月僅$6.4億。交易增長是輝達在6月發行$250億債券後，於週一起生效的最新一系列CDX投資等級指數中獲納入的主要原因。SpaceX發行規模相近的高評級債券後，也加入該系列。隨著輝達借款及基礎設施承諾增加，其違約保障成本今年已翻倍。

投資人利用信用違約交換契約，對沖集中持有AI債務的風險；銀行則藉買入保障降低借款人曝險，維持放款能力。CDX指數更換系列本身，加上美債殖利率升高，也促成指數利差擴大；這項機械性影響，與個別公司保障交易量及成本上升應分開看。單一公司避險交易增加，讓投資人有另一種方式管理橫跨投資等級、高收益及專案債務的AI建設融資風險。

即使上述交易順利完成，美國整體信用市場仍走弱。收盤時投資等級債利差小幅擴大，高收益債利差明顯擴大。按配息調整後的報酬計，LQD下跌1.15%，HYG下跌0.74%；損失也反映基礎利率上升。知情人士稱，Peloton正試探投資人對其首度發行約$8億擔保債的意願，指示性殖利率約8%，但尚未決定是否發行。其2024年一筆$10億槓桿貸款的利率，比參考基準高約6個百分點。Peloton的債券殖利率仍是推介階段的指示價；軟銀與Digital Drive則已有完成交易的定價。

其他發行人的條款各異。AerCap Funding完成$15億優先無擔保債定價，其中$7.5億為2030年到期、票息5.500%的債券，另$7.5億為2033年到期、票息5.875%的債券。AerCap Holdings及指定子公司提供全額保證；募集資金可用於飛機資產的融資或再融資、償債及一般用途。固定收益市場截止後，加拿大皇家銀行宣布發行$15億具不可存續或有資本條款的次順位債。該債至2031年10月1日支付4.67%利息，此後至2036年10月1日按複利CORRA加1.16個百分點計息。RBC自2031年起，經監管機關核准並提前30至60天通知後，可按面額贖回；交易預計10月1日完成交割。

Paramount Skydance規模大得多的收購融資，已進入直接向投資人推介的階段。先前拖延交易的訴訟和解後，銀行準備為其$1,100億收購華納兄弟探索公司的交易分銷債務；花旗安排在週四紐約時間上午10點30分與貸款投資人通話。融資組合包括約$300億投資等級債、$75億投資等級貸款，以及約$120億第二順位擔保債。架構先前已確定，新增的投資人電話會議則使各層級債務更接近由市場決定最終融資成本的時點。

通訊公司Bird.com完成一筆用途不同的小型融資。由摩根大通主導，該公司取得$4.5億資金，包括$4億定期貸款與$5,000萬循環額度；第一資本及花旗也支持這筆債務。執行長Robert Vis表示，借款將用來向現有股東及現任、前任員工發放股利，讓他們無須賣股即可取得資金。他指出，去年息稅折舊攤銷前盈餘為$1.65億，美國約占營收70%。這筆融資用於支付股利，並非擴充營運產能。

## 債務重整方案與主權融資進展

泰晤士水務的優先債權人準備提出更大讓步，以避免政府啟動特別接管。成員包括Elliott Investment Management、Silver Point Capital及Farallon Capital Management的London & Valley Water，在徵詢監管機關Ofwat及官員意見後，計畫最快於10月提交修訂方案。討論中的債務減記幅度由30%提高至約35%；擬投入股本由£33.5億增至約£35億，另有約£65.5億債務。數字仍在協商，但顯示債權人為取得這家負債逾£180億的公用事業控制權，願意承擔更大的潛在損失。

該團體另提議設立逾£10億專款，處理泰晤士水務的營運問題，比先前為取代部分績效罰款而提出的金額至少多£2億。依Ofwat制度，泰晤士水務因漏水、污水排放等指標未達標，至本世紀末預計可能承擔最多£8億的罰款；這些款項通常會透過降低帳單返還客戶。債權人主張，將資金用於修繕，更有助公司恢復投資等級信用評等。違反環境、飲用水或其他法規所生的法律罰款則屬另一回事，仍須支付。

整體方案也包括政府持有黃金股、加強監督，以及長達9年的整頓期，其間新股東不領取股利。國會議員反對債權人取得完全控制權，政府也正考慮特別接管。Teneo為泰晤士水務撰寫的分析估計，在政府控制下，A類債權人每£1債權可能僅收回約50便士，實際仍取決於營運表現。這是情境估計，並非已議定的回收率。修訂後的債權人方案與可能的政府接管之間如何取捨，使Ofwat的評估對債券持有人格外重要。

瑞士國會則通過一項對銀行資本證券影響更直接的決議。上議院以29票對16票支持修正案，要求瑞銀以高品質股權資本支持其外國子公司，金額最高達這些子公司價值的90%，接近政府最初提出的100%。瑞銀估計，措施將使其瑞士境內單位須額外持有約$160億普通股權第一類資本；高盛和花旗分析師估計負擔約$170億。

瑞銀原希望採用較寬鬆、更多仰賴或有可轉換AT1債的替代方案。投票結果使這條路變窄，市場預期新增AT1發行可能減少，現有瑞銀AT1債指示價格最多上漲0.3美分，至每$1面額98.36美分。瑞銀表示將繼續反對法案，認為其未處理瑞士信貸倒閉的成因，且會損害競爭力。下議院仍須表態；最終規則不太可能在2027年前出爐，也可能交由公民投票決定。

大宗商品交易商Radiant World的調查，則使債權人關注其提交法院的資產負債表中，應收款究竟能否收回。文件列有$10.07億貿易應收款，占主要營運公司$10.72億資產的大部分；其中前十大項目占應收款94%。彭博報導稱，列出的部分欠款公司否認有債務、與Radiant World關係密切，或無法在登記地址找到。Milla Sky Trading的登記代表表示，公司一年前已停止交易，也不知道有一筆$7,600萬債務；Vitol則表示，雖然帳上列有$1.007億應收款，但它與Radiant World的交易已結清。

Radiant World提供電子郵件截圖反駁上述疑慮，截圖看似顯示包括Milla Sky在內的數家公司確認欠款。另有$2.98億應收款，對應彭博報導所稱與Radiant World關係密切的公司。創辦人主張公司有償債能力，無須法院指定管理人；債權人瑞穗則指控詐欺，並要求任命管理人。各方說法相左，帳列應收款能否實際收回，仍是判斷債權人可取得多少清償的關鍵；資產負債表上的金額本身不代表將收到現金。

委內瑞拉主權債討論有兩國總統直接參與。美國國務卿Marco Rubio表示，川普總統與委內瑞拉代理總統Delcy Rodríguez在9月22日一場招待會討論債務重整，也談到未來選舉所需的制度建設。Rubio表示，美方希望協助穩定委內瑞拉經濟，但債務處理必須妥當；他指出，能運作的政黨、獨立媒體及可信的選舉機構，都是邁向選舉的必要條件。

委內瑞拉已違約的主權債與國營石油公司PDVSA債券合計約$600億。分析師估計，若計入累積利息及仲裁裁決等，更廣泛的負債達$1,500億至$2,000億；兩種金額的差異，關係到日後不同索償人如何分配回收款。委內瑞拉5月宣布將著手重整自2017年起違約的債務，美洲開發銀行則正爭取核准一筆$25億貸款，但部分董事反對。川普與Rodríguez的對話增加了政治參與，尚未確定債權人條款，也未使這筆多邊貸款獲得核准。

匈牙利本幣債券則呈現不同的外資需求。央行自2028年起將長期通膨目標降至2.5%一事早已為市場知悉；新的估計則量化了與歐元趨同預期相關的資金流入。德意志銀行計算，今年迄今外資買入$135億匈牙利債券，其中$100億發生在4月選舉後。匈牙利債務管理機關指出，截至8月底，外資持有比重達34%，為2019年以來最高。該國10年期公債殖利率約5.64%，低於波蘭的6.16%與羅馬尼亞的7.29%。

外資需求仍取決於財政政策能否落實。匈牙利2026年赤字預計占GDP的7.5%，投資人正關注2027年預算及中期計畫。約€160億遭凍結的歐盟資金若獲撥付，可能提供支撐，但目前仍未實現。另在政府採取法治相關措施後，歐盟執委會週三提議解除對€42億凝聚政策資金的凍結。這是爭取資金的新進展，並不等於款項已到位，或更廣泛的財政調整已完成。

中國人民銀行處理的是較迫近的資金時程。人行宣布，9月28日至10月8日期間，每日可提供最多人民幣1兆元、約$1,490億的隔夜逆回購，但未指定個別操作日或借款成本。銀行間債券市場預定因中秋節於9月25日至27日休市，並因國慶節於10月1日至7日休市。這項臨時安排旨在滿足假期及交割中斷期間銀行體系的現金需求，並非調整政策利率。

固定收益市場完成收盤後，美中貿易又有新進展。財政部長Scott Bessent表示，在習近平主席訪問華府前，他與中國副總理何立峰會晤後，華府與北京於9月23日同意把釜山協議延長至1月10日。他說雙方也討論，是否能以一項更大規模的協議取代一系列較小協議。延期降低現有框架近期失效的風險；更廣泛協議的條款，仍待兩國領導人敲定。

## 後續市場觀察

週四的財政部回購，將揭示20至30年期公債在已公布的$60億上限中實際買入多少，以及投資人願意以什麼價格出售。5年期標售出現3.1個基點尾差後，7年期標售將另行檢驗需求。兩項結果可觀察，週三新發中天期公債所需的殖利率讓步，在供給延伸至更長期限時是否仍會持續。

美國勞動數據將檢驗Barr認為就業風險已減輕的判斷。9月24日初領失業救濟金人數預計為20.1萬人，前值19.6萬人；續領人數預計為175萬人，前值173萬人。週五的耐久財報告，整體訂單預計下降0.4%，但扣除運輸後預計增加0.6%，扣除飛機的非國防資本財訂單預計增加0.5%。PMI顯示製造業與服務業訂單均加快，這份報告的細項組合因而重要。9月密西根大學消費者信心終值調查中，1年通膨預期預計為4.6%、5年為3.4%，可從家庭角度觀察物價壓力是否持續。聯準會地區銀行總裁John Williams和Tom Barkin也預定週四發言。

美伊談判仍須接受實際能源供應的檢驗。Pezeshkian就制裁、封鎖及荷莫茲海峽通行提出的條件，使航道何時重開仍無定論。相較再次宣布會談，船舶持續通行及出口穩定恢復，才會更明顯改變能源市場背景。新延長的貿易框架之後，川普與習近平的峰會將顯示，兩國領導人能否在1月10日前，就關稅、投資或科技達成更廣泛條款。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off across the coupon curve on September 23 as oil rebounded, a strong U.S. business survey strengthened the case for further Federal Reserve tightening, and a weak $70 billion 5-year auction intensified the decline. In Bloomberg’s dated yield histories, the 10-year yield rose 15.2 basis points to 5.115% and the 5-year climbed 16.7 basis points to 5.004%. The auction cleared at 5.033%, 3.1 basis points above its when-issued yield. The 5-year yield crossed 5% in trading for the first time since 2007, reversing the previous session’s relief at the short end.

The energy move changed the day’s starting point. Brent futures finished at $103.08 a barrel, up 3.86%, after the prior day’s diplomatic hopes had helped push prices lower. Iran’s president maintained conditions on passage through the Strait of Hormuz, leaving a substantial obstacle to restored supply. The September flash U.S. composite purchasing managers’ index then reached 58.4, its highest since July 2021, with stronger orders and a sharp rise in input costs. Fed Governor Michael Barr said inflation risks had increased while labor-market risks had receded. Those developments gave the auction weakness a broader inflation and policy backdrop.

The rise in yields reached other government-bond markets: Wednesday’s trading account put German and British 10-year yields up 9 and 11 basis points, respectively. The dollar strengthened, the S&P 500 fell, and U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly while high-yield spreads widened noticeably. Companies still obtained financing, but at demanding prices. SoftBank completed roughly $11 billion of dollar and euro junk-bond issuance to fund its AI ambitions, paying its highest dollar-bond yields on record. The contrast between successful placement and expensive borrowing was a second defining feature of the session.

## U.S. Growth, Fed Policy and Auction Demand Reprice Treasuries

Oil began Wednesday with a less reassuring trajectory than it had shown during the preceding session’s U.S.-Iran diplomacy. Brent moved back above $100 a barrel. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the United Nations General Assembly that his country would not allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while sanctions and a U.S. blockade remained. He said Iran was ready to resume discussions, but his conditions underscored the distance between another round of talks and a reopening of a critical energy route.

The U.S. administration was also examining fuel-supply measures at home. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said it was working with refiners to curb diesel exports voluntarily. The White House denied a report that it was preparing a 90-day export ban. Those statements did not establish a change in shipments, but they showed how elevated fuel costs were drawing a policy response alongside diplomacy. Brent’s rise to $103.08 at the 5 p.m. New York fixed-income cutoff restored immediate pressure to an inflation outlook that had briefly benefited from cheaper crude.

The September flash S&P Global survey brought a separate source of pressure. Its U.S. composite output index rose to 58.4 from 56.0 in August, above a 55.2 forecast and the highest reading in more than five years. Manufacturing increased to 57.0 from 53.9, against a 53.6 consensus, while services rose to 58.7 from 56.5, against 56.0 expected. Both sides of the private economy accelerated. That breadth made the release more consequential for rates than a strong headline produced by one sector.

Orders and capacity measures reinforced the message. The new-orders index reached 58.2 from 55.2, its highest since March 2022, with gains in manufacturing and services. Backlogs were the largest since May 2022, and supplier delivery delays were the most widespread since July 2022. Employment increased at its fastest pace in more than four years. The input-price index jumped to 66.4 from 59.9, the highest since October 2022; businesses cited fuel and transport costs, while many also reported faster wage growth. Stronger demand was arriving alongside constraints on supplying it.

S&P Global said the survey was consistent with roughly 5% annualized GDP growth. The Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow estimate was running at 5.1%, compared with actual growth of 1.5% in Q2. The PMI remains a preliminary measure of the breadth of business conditions, rather than a realized GDP result. Its combination of faster output, orders, hiring and costs nonetheless offered a concrete reason for investors to reassess how soon tighter policy might slow the economy.

Barr gave that reassessment an explicit Fed voice. The governor, a voting member of the rate-setting committee, said risks to the inflation target had increased as risks to the labor market had receded. He judged further policy adjustments likely to be needed to return inflation to 2% in a timely way. The committee had unanimously raised its target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% the previous week, and 16 of 18 policymakers had projected at least one more increase before year-end. Reuters interpreted Barr’s remarks as suggesting he saw a need for at least two more increases, though he did not specify their timing.

Short-rate futures put the chance of another increase at the October 27-28 meeting at about 70% after his remarks, up from roughly 55% earlier Wednesday. In the broader rates market, swaps fully reflected three quarter-point moves over the next year, with substantial hedging for a fourth. The measures describe different horizons, but both showed the market assigning more weight to a continuing tightening cycle after the survey and Barr’s comments.

The White House disputed the need for that course. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett argued that a recent annualized core inflation rate of 2% did not warrant further increases. He criticized Fed officials who had not been appointed by President Donald Trump for calling for more tightening and said Chair Kevin Warsh was managing an unusually partisan central bank. Hassett singled out former chair Jerome Powell and Barr. Warsh, Powell and Barr had all voted for the previous week’s increase, along with the rest of the committee. Hassett’s criticism established a political disagreement over the data and policy response, while Barr’s remarks supplied the day’s detailed new Fed condition.

The afternoon 5-year auction then tested demand in a market already selling off. The $70 billion sale cleared at a yield of 5.033%, compared with a 5.002% when-issued reference. Its 3.1-basis-point tail was the second-worst 5-year result in Bloomberg records since 2018, surpassed only by a June 2022 auction. Bid-to-cover was 2.21; indirect bidders took 54.3%, direct bidders 29.9%, and dealers 15.8%. The clearing yield was the highest for this tenor since 2006. The auction result was a distinct acceleration of the day’s rate move, not its sole cause.

The 5-year yield rose as much as 20 basis points during the session, crossing the 4.99% high reached in 2023. Bloomberg’s trading account described the 10-year yield rising almost 17 basis points to 5.13% at one observation and the 30-year trading around 5.4%. In the same-date Bloomberg yield histories, the 2-year rose 14.2 basis points to 4.898%, the 5-year 16.7 to 5.004%, the 10-year 15.2 to 5.115%, and the 30-year 10.0 to 5.401%. The 2s30s slope narrowed 4.2 basis points to 50.3 as shorter maturities absorbed more of the adjustment.

Inflation-linked bonds locate most of the 10-year move in real rates. The 10-year TIPS yield rose 13.2 basis points to 2.77%, while the matching breakeven increased 2.0 basis points to 2.345%. Oil remained a material inflation concern, but the same-source decomposition shows that Wednesday’s nominal repricing was predominantly a rise in the real yield investors demanded. The combination is consistent with a stronger growth reading, a higher expected policy path and a greater cost of holding duration.

The move was visible beyond bonds. The Dollar Index rose 0.56% to 101.10, while a separate Bloomberg dollar gauge gained 0.6% and reached its highest since late July. The S&P 500 declined 0.75%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.84%, and the semiconductor index fell 1.21%. Gold futures dropped 1.33% to $4,318.40. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF fell 1.6% to $80.46, a record closing low. Its year-to-date total return, including distributions, was down 4.8%, compared with a 7.7% fall in its share price, a distinction that matters when assessing the cost borne by holders.

Housing finance had already tightened before Wednesday’s Treasury close. The Mortgage Bankers Association reported that the contract rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage rose 15 basis points to 7.12% in the week ended September 18, its highest since May 2024. Total applications fell 1.5% after a 4.1% decline in the preceding week. The mortgage market index slipped to 227.3 from 230.8, the refinance index to 611.0 from 627.1, and the purchase index to 154.9 from 156.2. The 5-year adjustable mortgage rate moved the other way, falling 13 basis points to 6.1%. The fixed-rate increase and weaker applications show the housing constraint already in place as Treasury yields rose again.

The Treasury separately announced that it would buy up to $6 billion of bonds maturing in 20 to 30 years on Thursday under Secretary Scott Bessent’s expanded buyback program. The maximum is triple the $2 billion size originally communicated in August. Long bonds extended their decline after the announcement, and the reported 30-year yield reached a session high of 5.38% at that point. At the previous expanded operation, the Treasury purchased about $5.2 billion against a $6 billion maximum after investors offered $10.5 billion of securities; officials cited a lack of competitive bids for the unused capacity. The Institute of International Finance argued Wednesday that secondary-market purchases might offer temporary relief but would not resolve the fiscal forces behind rising debt. Thursday’s authorization sets a ceiling, with the actual purchase amount still to be determined.

## Global Activity and Central Banks Confront the Energy Shock

The OECD’s interim outlook widened the policy issue beyond the United States. It raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 2.9% from 2.8%, after 3.4% growth in 2025, but lowered the 2027 projection to 3.0% from 3.1%. It lifted its G20 inflation forecasts to 4.1% this year from 4.0% and to 3.6% next year from 3.1%. Its 2027 inflation projections rose for every G20 economy except China and Saudi Arabia. AI investment supported the nearer-term growth estimate, while a more persistent energy shock weakened the later outlook.

The OECD projected one further Fed increase this year, modest additional moves in the euro area, Australia and South Korea, and further tightening in Japan. It expected the Bank of England and Bank of Canada to hold for now. For the U.S., it forecast growth of 2.2% in 2026 and 2.1% in 2027, with inflation of 3.6% and 2.6%. Its adverse scenario combined energy-market stress, a strong El Niño, higher government-bond yields and disappointing AI returns. Together, those shocks could reduce 2027 global growth by 0.7 percentage point and raise inflation by 1.1 points. That scenario showed how a higher cost of capital could compound supply and investment disappointments; it was not the organization’s central forecast.

The euro area’s own September activity release strengthened the near-term side of that picture. Its composite PMI rose to 53.1 from 52.0, against a forecast decline to 51.7, reaching its highest in more than three years. Services improved unexpectedly. Germany’s activity grew at its fastest pace since October 2025, and France expanded at its quickest in more than two years. S&P Global’s Chris Williamson attributed part of manufacturing’s strength to AI and defense spending and reported better order books across manufacturing and services. The survey described an economy still expanding despite higher energy and borrowing costs.

That resilience did not support the euro on Wednesday. The currency fell as low as $1.1409 against the dollar, near a two-month low, as traders increased downside hedges. Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation data cited in market reporting showed roughly 60% of euro options notional positioned for weakness since the latest Fed meeting, compared with a nearly even split after the ECB’s increase. The weighted-average expiry of bearish exposure had also lengthened by more than 10%. U.S. growth and rate expectations were strengthening at the same time that expensive energy threatened the euro area’s later outlook. Deutsche Bank analysts offered a counterview, expecting resilient global growth and dollar-specific risks to limit an extended euro decline.

ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane qualified the inflation concern. He said the energy surge had not yet produced significant wage pressure, reducing evidence that the headline shock was being embedded through pay. But he described energy prices as tracking the ECB’s adverse scenario through the middle of 2027 before returning toward its baseline. Natural-gas storage was about 70%, or 16 percentage points below its historical average. Euro-area inflation had exceeded 3% in August, and some economists expected it to reach 4% by year-end.

Lane also distinguished observed market prices from a straightforward count of expected ECB increases. Pricing appeared to imply another three or four moves beyond the June and September hikes, but after removing risk premia, he said the implied peak was only just above 3% next year before declining by end-2027. He regarded that as consistent with about two further hikes. His wage assessment tempered one route to persistent inflation without removing the risk from energy prices and low gas inventories.

Britain faced a different combination of slowing activity and fiscal exposure. The OECD forecast U.K. growth of 1.1% in 2026 and 1.0% in 2027, with inflation averaging 3.1% and 2.6%. It saw the BOE holding its 3.75% policy rate until mid-2027 before cutting by a quarter point, while urging stronger efforts to contain and redirect government spending. Economists estimated that higher interest costs and inflation had already halved Chancellor John Healey’s £23.6 billion cushion against the fiscal rules.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham added a political dimension ahead of the October 28 budget. He stood by earlier remarks that Britain should not be “in hock” to bond markets, saying the country had left itself overexposed while arguing for a more productive state. His government faces defense and social-spending ambitions as borrowing runs above prior projections. The reported 30-year gilt yield was 5.76%, below a near-6% peak the previous week. Wednesday’s rise in British yields occurred within a wider global selloff; Burnham’s comments and the OECD’s warning sharpened the fiscal question the budget will have to answer.

South Africa made a completed policy choice. Its six-member monetary policy committee unanimously raised the benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 7.25%, the outcome expected by 19 of 22 economists surveyed by Bloomberg. Governor Lesetja Kganyago said the bank had to bring inflation back to its 3% target as the shock faded. August inflation edged up to 4.4% from 4.3%. The bank raised its average inflation forecast for 2026 to 4.4% from 4.0% and for 2027 to 4.0% from 3.8%, while increasing its oil assumptions to $90 a barrel this year from $82 and to $80 next year from $75.

Officials had discussed holding and a 50-basis-point increase as well as the chosen quarter-point move. Kganyago described policy as marginally restrictive before the decision and warned that large, sustained shocks were more likely to produce second-round effects. The bank’s adverse scenarios, involving higher global rates or domestic inflation expectations, called for one or two more increases than otherwise. In Johannesburg afternoon trading, the rand extended its decline to about 16.39 per dollar, down 1.3%, and the 10-year government yield rose 9 basis points to 8.90%. The unanimous vote and revised forecasts gave the increase a firmer inflation rationale than the size alone conveyed.

Bank Indonesia held at 5.75% for a third meeting, as 33 of 36 surveyed economists expected, and used currency-market incentives to address external pressure. Under Governor Destry Damayanti, it cut premiums for conventional hedging swaps on portfolio investment by up to 25% and for domestic nondeliverable forwards by up to 30%. Longer-held funds receive larger discounts. The bank continued offshore and onshore intervention, including secondary-market government-bond purchases. The rupiah strengthened 0.4% to about 17,800 per dollar and local bonds held earlier gains after the decision.

Destry said the existing rate was adequate for stability but acknowledged oil above $100 in the trading context, higher global inflation and the prospect of another Fed increase. Indonesia’s August inflation was 3.2%, near the top of its 1.5%-3.5% target range, while bank lending grew 13.65% from a year earlier, above the bank’s 8%-12% expectation. Lombard Odier’s Homin Lee still forecast a quarter-point increase in December if energy uncertainty and Fed tightening persisted. The hold therefore relied on capital-retention incentives and intervention while leaving a rate response conditional on continued pressure.

Singapore reported another distinct Asian inflation observation. Core consumer prices rose 2.2% from a year earlier in August, their highest rate since September 2024 and in line with survey expectations. Food, retail and services inflation accelerated; headline inflation was 2.3%, and utilities and other fuels rose 6.1%. The Monetary Authority of Singapore and the trade ministry judged risks tilted upward as oil, weather and imported costs worked through supply chains. The MAS forecast core inflation of 1.5%-2.5% this year and moderation from around mid-2027. Its next decision, due in mid-October, will assess whether those pressures require a further currency-policy adjustment.

Japan’s bond market was closed for the Silver Week holiday, leaving its response to Wednesday’s global yield rise for the Thursday reopening. The yen completed a four-day decline against the dollar, renewing concern about currency intervention and the inflation effect of a weaker exchange rate after the BOJ’s recent increase to 1.25%. Eastspring Investments offered a separate assessment of where global duration demand could move. Portfolio manager Rong Ren Goh said a 30-year Japanese government bond yielding above 4%, swapped into dollars or another developed-market currency, could produce a currency-hedged yield 100-200 basis points above a comparable bond in that currency. He cited a Japanese 2s30s curve steeper than 200 basis points, against an average near 80 in other core developed markets. Eastspring was building ultra-long Japanese exposure through high-quality corporate and Samurai bonds while adding shorter-dated dollar debt. Those are the manager’s strategy and yield comparisons; Japanese trading after the holiday will provide the next market observation.

## AI Borrowing Clears at High Cost as Credit Hedging Grows

SoftBank converted preliminary demand into borrowing terms on Wednesday. The Japanese group raised roughly $11 billion across dollar and euro junk bonds for its AI plans, becoming the world’s largest corporate junk-bond borrower in Bloomberg’s compilation. A $1 billion 3.5-year dollar tranche yielded 8.625%, a $4.5 billion 5.5-year tranche yielded 9.25%, and a $4.5 billion tranche due in 7.5 years yielded 9.75%. It also sold €1 billion in four- and six-year notes, with the longer euro tranche yielding 8%. The dollar yields were the highest SoftBank had paid in that market, while the longer euro yield set a record for its borrowing at that tenor.

Orders for the $10 billion dollar portion exceeded $30 billion in Asian afternoon indications, allowing SoftBank to lower yields from initial ranges. The book showed that a very large speculative-grade financing could be placed, yet its final cost remained steep as benchmark Treasury yields rose. SoftBank’s commitments to OpenAI approach $65 billion, and it has used other secured and bridge financing alongside the new unsecured bonds. Goldman Sachs credit strategists put global AI-related debt issuance above $575 billion in 2026. The price of insuring SoftBank debt against default reached its highest this month since April 2025, showing that strong bond orders did not erase concern about the scale of its exposure.

A smaller construction financing drew an equally high headline yield for different reasons. A developer sponsored by Blue Owl Capital affiliates, Cedarwood Investment Group and PowerHouse Data Centers raised $1.1 billion in five-year junk bonds for the Digital Drive data-center campus near Richmond, Virginia. The notes priced at 98.5 cents on the dollar to yield 9.25%, roughly 2.7 percentage points above the average yield on similarly rated debt. Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Deutsche Bank ran the sale.

The financing will add computing capacity to a 76-megawatt facility fully leased to CoreWeave under a 15-year, $2.94 billion contract. Operations are expected to begin in 2027-2028. S&P assigned the bonds a BB- rating and identified reliance on a single speculative-grade tenant as the principal risk. The long lease supports projected revenue, but the project still needs funding before operations begin, and the tenant’s credit quality shaped the yield demanded by investors.

Hedging activity around established AI borrowers has also expanded. Market participants traded protection on $6.9 billion of Nvidia debt over the latest six months, compared with $640 million in the preceding six, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices’ Nicholas Godec citing DTCC data. That increase was the primary reason Nvidia entered the latest CDX investment-grade index series, effective Monday, after its $25 billion June bond sale. SpaceX joined the series as well after selling a similarly sized high-grade deal. Nvidia protection costs have doubled this year amid its borrowing and infrastructure commitments.

Investors have sought the swaps to hedge concentrated AI-debt exposure, while banks have used protection to reduce borrower exposure and maintain lending capacity. The CDX index roll itself, together with higher Treasury yields, contributed to index widening. That mechanical effect is separate from the rise in trading and protection costs for individual names. The growth of single-name hedging gives investors another way to manage the credit consequences of an AI buildout that is being financed across high-grade, junk and project debt.

Broad U.S. credit weakened even as these deals cleared. Investment-grade spreads widened modestly and high-yield spreads widened noticeably at the close. On a distribution-adjusted return basis, LQD fell 1.15% and HYG 0.74%; the losses also reflect higher underlying rates. Peloton was sounding investors on a possible $800 million debut secured bond with an indicated yield around 8%, according to people familiar with the discussions. It had not decided to proceed. Its earlier $1 billion leveraged loan in 2024 carried a rate about 6 percentage points above its benchmark. The proposed bond yield remains a marketing indication, while SoftBank and Digital Drive provide completed prices.

Other issuers supplied different financing terms. AerCap Funding priced $1.5 billion of senior unsecured notes, split between $750 million of 5.500% debt due 2030 and $750 million of 5.875% debt due 2033. AerCap Holdings and specified subsidiaries fully guarantee the notes; proceeds may finance or refinance aircraft assets, repay debt or fund general purposes. After the fixed-income cutoff, Royal Bank of Canada announced $1.5 billion of non-viability contingent-capital subordinated debentures. They pay 4.67% until October 1, 2031, then compounded CORRA plus 1.16 percentage points until October 1, 2036. RBC may redeem at par from 2031 with supervisory approval and 30-60 days’ notice; closing is expected October 1.

Paramount Skydance’s much larger acquisition financing advanced to direct investor marketing. Citigroup scheduled loan-investor calls for Thursday at 10:30 a.m. New York time as banks prepared to distribute debt for the $110 billion Warner Bros. Discovery takeover after lawsuits delaying the transaction were settled. The package includes about $30 billion of investment-grade bonds, $7.5 billion of investment-grade loans and roughly $12 billion of second-lien bonds. Its structure was already established; the newly scheduled calls bring the transaction closer to the point at which investors will set clearing costs across its different ranks of debt.

Messaging company Bird.com completed a smaller financing with a different use of proceeds. It raised $450 million led by JPMorgan, comprising a $400 million term loan and a $50 million revolving facility, with Capital One and Citigroup also backing the debt. Chief Executive Robert Vis said the borrowing would fund a dividend to existing shareholders and current and former employees, providing liquidity without their selling shares. He put last year’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization at $165 million and said the U.S. generated about 70% of revenue. The financing funds a payout rather than new operating capacity.

## Restructuring Proposals and Sovereign Funding Develop

Thames Water’s senior creditors were preparing a larger concession package to avert government special administration. London & Valley Water, whose members include Elliott Investment Management, Silver Point Capital and Farallon Capital Management, plans to submit a revised proposal as soon as October after seeking feedback from regulator Ofwat and officials. The debt write-down under discussion rises to about 35% from 30%. Proposed equity increases from £3.35 billion to around £3.5 billion, alongside roughly £6.55 billion of debt. The figures remain under negotiation, but they show creditors accepting a larger prospective loss in pursuit of control of a utility with more than £18 billion of debt.

The group also proposes more than £1 billion for a dedicated fund to address Thames’s operational failures, at least £200 million more than it previously offered in place of some performance penalties. Under Ofwat’s system, Thames is expected to incur as much as £800 million of penalties by decade-end for missed targets on leaks, sewage spills and other measures; those amounts would normally be returned to customers through lower bills. Creditors argue that spending the money on repairs would give the company a better path back to investment grade. Legal fines for breaches of environmental, drinking-water or other rules remain separate and payable.

The broader proposal includes a government golden share, more oversight and a nine-year turnaround during which new owners would take no dividends. Lawmakers have objected to creditors gaining full control, and the government is considering special administration. A Teneo analysis prepared for Thames estimated that Class A creditors could recover as little as about 50 pence per pound under government control, depending on operating performance. That is a scenario estimate, not an agreed recovery. The contrast between the revised creditor package and possible administration gives Ofwat’s assessment immediate significance for bondholders.

Swiss lawmakers made a decision with a more direct effect on bank capital securities. The upper house voted 29-16 for an amendment requiring UBS to back its foreign subsidiaries with high-quality equity equal to as much as 90% of their value. That is close to the government’s original 100% proposal. UBS estimated the measure would require about $16 billion of additional common equity tier 1 capital at its domestic unit; Goldman Sachs and Citigroup analysts put the burden around $17 billion.

UBS had sought a less onerous alternative relying more heavily on contingent-convertible AT1 debt. That route narrowed after the vote, and existing UBS AT1 bonds rose as much as 0.3 cent to 98.36 cents on indicative prices as the prospect of additional issuance receded. UBS said it would continue opposing the bill, arguing that the outcome failed to address the causes of Credit Suisse’s collapse and would damage competitiveness. The lower house must still take a position. A final rule is unlikely before 2027 and could ultimately be put to a public vote.

An investigation into commodity trader Radiant World raised a different question for creditors: the collectability of assets presented in its court-filed balance sheet. That document lists $1.007 billion of trade receivables, which account for most of the main operating company’s $1.072 billion of assets. The 10 largest entries represent 94% of the receivables. Bloomberg reported that several listed debtors denied owing money, were closely connected to Radiant World or could not be located at their stated addresses. Milla Sky Trading’s registered representative said it had stopped trading a year earlier and denied knowledge of a $76 million debt; Vitol said its transactions with Radiant World had been settled despite a listed $100.7 million receivable.

Radiant World disputed the implication by providing screenshots of emails that appeared to confirm debts from several companies, including Milla Sky. A further $298 million of receivables were listed against companies described in Bloomberg’s reporting as closely connected to Radiant World. Its founder has argued the company is solvent and does not need judicial managers, while creditor Mizuho has alleged fraud and sought their appointment. The competing accounts leave repayment of the claimed receivables central to determining what creditors can recover; the balance-sheet entries alone do not establish cash that will be collected.

Venezuela’s sovereign debt discussions gained direct presidential involvement. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump and interim President Delcy Rodríguez had discussed restructuring at a September 22 reception, alongside the institutional work required for future elections. Rubio said Washington wanted to help stabilize Venezuela’s economy, but that debt treatment had to be carried out properly. He identified functioning political parties, independent media and credible electoral institutions as necessary steps toward elections.

Venezuelan sovereign and PDVSA bonds in default total about $60 billion. Analysts estimate broader liabilities, including accrued interest and arbitration awards, at $150 billion-$200 billion. The distinction matters to any eventual division of recoveries among claimants. Venezuela announced in May that it would begin restructuring debt that has been in default since 2017, and the Inter-American Development Bank is working toward approval of a $2.5 billion loan against resistance from some board members. The Trump-Rodríguez discussion adds political engagement but establishes neither creditor terms nor approval for the proposed multilateral financing.

Hungarian local bonds offered a contrasting account of foreign demand. The central bank’s lower long-run inflation target of 2.5% from 2028 was already known; new estimates put a scale on the inflows associated with the euro-convergence narrative. Deutsche Bank calculated $13.5 billion of foreign purchases year to date, including $10 billion after the April election. Hungary’s debt agency put foreign holdings at 34% by August’s end, their highest share since 2019. The 10-year government yield was about 5.64%, below Poland’s 6.16% and Romania’s 7.29%.

That demand still depends on fiscal delivery. Hungary’s 2026 deficit is projected at 7.5% of GDP, and investors are focused on the 2027 budget and medium-term plan. Release of about €16 billion in frozen EU funds could provide support, but remains prospective. Separately, the European Commission proposed Wednesday to unblock €4.2 billion of cohesion financing after the government moved on rule-of-law measures. The proposal is a fresh step toward funding, distinct from receipt of the money or completion of the broader fiscal adjustment.

China addressed a more immediate funding calendar. The People’s Bank of China announced that overnight reverse repos of up to 1 trillion yuan, about $149 billion, per day would be available from September 28 through October 8. It did not specify individual operation days or the borrowing cost. The interbank bond market is scheduled to close September 25-27 for Mid-Autumn Festival and October 1-7 for National Day. The temporary facility is intended to meet banking-system cash needs across those holiday and settlement interruptions, rather than to change the policy rate.

A U.S.-China trade development arrived after the completed fixed-income close. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington and Beijing had agreed on September 23 to extend their Busan agreement through January 10 following his meeting with Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of President Xi Jinping’s Washington visit. Bessent said they also discussed whether a larger deal could replace a series of smaller agreements. The extension reduces the immediate risk of the framework expiring, while the terms of any broader accord remain for the leaders to settle.

## Forward Market Significance

Thursday’s Treasury buyback will show how much of the announced $6 billion maximum for 20- to 30-year debt the department purchases and at what prices investors offer bonds. A 7-year auction provides a separate test of demand after the 5-year sale’s 3.1-basis-point tail. Those results can show whether the concession required for Wednesday’s new intermediate-maturity supply persists as issuance moves farther along the curve.

U.S. labor data will test Barr’s judgment that employment risks have receded. Initial jobless claims on September 24 are expected at 201,000 after 196,000, with continuing claims at 1.750 million after 1.730 million. Friday’s durable-goods report is expected to show a 0.4% headline decline but gains of 0.6% excluding transportation and 0.5% in nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft. That composition will matter after the PMI reported faster orders across both manufacturing and services. The final September Michigan survey carries expected one-year inflation expectations of 4.6% and five-year expectations of 3.4%, bringing a household measure to the question of persistent price pressure. Fed Presidents John Williams and Tom Barkin are also scheduled to speak Thursday.

The U.S.-Iran negotiations face a physical supply test. Pezeshkian’s conditions on sanctions, the blockade and Hormuz passage leave the route’s reopening unresolved despite renewed talks. Sustained transit and export flows would change the energy backdrop more decisively than a further meeting announcement. The Trump-Xi summit follows the newly extended trade framework and will show whether the leaders can agree on broader tariff, investment or technology terms before January 10.

Japan’s return from holiday will provide the first local bond-market response to Wednesday’s Treasury decline and a further test of the yen after its four-day slide. Norges Bank’s closely divided rate decision and the Riksbank’s expected hold are due Thursday with updated forecasts; a Norwegian increase to 4.5% alongside an unchanged Swedish rate of 1.75% would widen their policy-rate gap to 275 basis points. For credit, Paramount’s investor calls will begin testing the market for its large multi-rank debt package, while Thames Water’s proposed October revision must persuade Ofwat and the government that larger creditor concessions can deliver a viable alternative to special administration.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries sold off across the coupon curve on September 23. The 10-year yield rose 15.2 basis points to 5.115%, while the 5-year climbed 16.7 basis points to 5.004%, crossing 5% in trading for the first time since 2007. Brent rebounded to $103.08 a barrel as conditions on passage through the Strait of Hormuz left supply uncertain. The September U.S. composite PMI reached 58.4, with stronger orders and sharply higher input costs, and Fed Governor Michael Barr said inflation risks had increased while labor-market risks had receded. A $70 billion 5-year auction then cleared 3.1 basis points above its when-issued yield, intensifying the decline.

The dollar strengthened, equities fell, and U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads widened. Financing remained available at a high cost: SoftBank placed roughly $11 billion of dollar and euro junk bonds for its AI plans while paying its highest dollar-bond yields on record.
